title: Recovery Evaluation App for Comprehensive Treatment support – a prospective feasibility study
summary:
After major operations, there are well-established care pathways that are intended to help patients recover faster and more safely. These include structured measures before, during and after surgery, as well as good, easy-to-understand information for patients. In everyday practice, however, it is not always easy to provide all information clearly and at the right time. Digital applications could help to support patients more effectively and reduce the workload of the care team. For this purpose, an app has been developed that offers information, short learning content, daily goals and interactive functions. Scientific evaluation by patients is still pending.
The study aims to find out how understandable, helpful and user-friendly this app is perceived to be by patients who have already undergone a relevant operation and completed their recovery. In addition, the study will examine whether conducting such a survey study is generally feasible.
In this study, adult patients will be invited who underwent surgery at the University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf within the past three years and have already completed their recovery. They will be given access to a demo version of the app. They will then complete a one-time questionnaire. Among other aspects, they will rate the app’s usability, its perceived benefit for their own recovery, individual content elements, and any technical problems. They can also provide suggestions for improvement. Participation is voluntary and will not affect medical care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Previous surgical procedure (pancreas, liver, esophagus, or sarcoma) performed within a standardized ERAS protocol (within the last 36 months), with a signed biobank consent form available (PV3548).
• Capacity to provide informed consent.
• Agreement to be contacted and to participate in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
• Severe cognitive impairments.
• Language barriers if the app and questionnaire are not understandable.
• No possibility to use digital devices (smartphone, tablet, or PC).
